item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Crosses 4 Million Sales in 72 Hours
item.dc:creator: Ravi Sinha
item.description: The action RPG has also become the 14th most-played title in Steam's history after peaking at over 833,000 concurrent players.
item.content:encoded:
After debuting with exceptionally strong concurrent player numbers on Steam and rave reviews, S-Game’s Phantom Blade Zero has sold over four million copies. Even better, it achieved this milestone within 72 hours.

The action RPG topped three million wishlists across PS5 and PC in September, and reportedly sold close to one million before launch (over that figure when accounting for other storefronts). Granted, it’s far below Game Science’s Black Myth: Wukong, which sold ten million copies in its first four days.

But it’s still an impressive milestone, especially compared to contemporaries like Control Resonant, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and The Blood of Dawnwalker. On Steam, Phantom Blade Zero set a new peak concurrent player record yesterday at 833,921 and became the 14th highest-played title in the platform’s history. Not bad for what’s essentially a relatively unknown (if not new) IP.

For more details on Phantom Blade Zero, check out our review. We gave it a 9 for its combat, which starts a little slow but ramps up after the opening hours, whether it’s weapon selection or boss fights. The presentation is top-notch throughout, while the somewhat limited exploration (at least in the first two regions) expands significantly with interesting side quests and hidden bosses. Check out all our tips for succeeding and surviving in the Wulin here.

item.title: Dark Soul 2 and 3 Taken Offline “Temporarily” Due to “Server Issue,” Says FromSoftware
item.dc:creator: Ravi Sinha
item.description: There's currently no estimated time for when servers will return, though the developer will update players when it has more details.
item.content:encoded:
Remember when FromSoftware took down servers for its Dark Souls games, and uncertainty reigned over whether they would ever return? It’s happened again, this time for Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3.

This is apparently due to a “server issue” which affects all platforms. The developer said it will update players on “server restoration time” once it has more “information.” At the very least, this is temporary, though one’s interpretation may vary. Either way, if you’ve been having a blast in co-op for either title, you’ll need to postpone those playthroughs until the foreseeable future.

Fortunately, the outage hasn’t affected Elden Ring, FromSoftware’s most recent Souls-like title. If you haven’t given it a go (and you really should), check out our reviews of the base game and Shadow of the Erdtree expansion to learn more. Elden Ring Nightreign, built for three-player co-op, is also available, though it offers more of a rogue-lite structure. You can learn more about it and its DLC, The Forsaken Hollows.

Either title might help pass the time for The Duskbloods, especially since it was delayed from 2026 to 2027 to incorporate feedback from the recent closed beta. A more definitive release window has yet to be announced, and it’s unknown whether there will be another beta, but stay tuned for updates.
